records.source: וַיַּשְׁכֵּם֩ יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ בַּבֹּ֜קֶר וַיִּסְע֣וּ מֵֽהַשִּׁטִּ֗ים וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ עַד־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן ה֖וּא וְכָל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּלִ֥נוּ שָׁ֖ם טֶ֥רֶם יַעֲבֹֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: And rose early Joshua in the morning, and they set out from the Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all [the] sons of Israel, and they lodged there before they crossed over.
pieces: Joshua got up early in the morning. He and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, and they stopped there for the night before crossing over.

L.1: And Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and they lodged there before they crossed over.

R.1: Early in the morning, Joshua and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left Shittim and went to the Jordan River. They camped there before they crossed the river.

decisions.choice: Shittim: Israel's last camp east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The name means "acacia trees". Israel camped there on the plains of Moab across the river from Jericho (Numbers 25:1; 33:49, where it is called Abel-shittim), and the two spies were sent out from there (2:1).

decisions.choice: rose early in the morning: set out without delay
decisions.reason: The phrase often marks a prompt start to an important task (Genesis 22:3; Exodus 24:4; Joshua 6:12). Joshua acts at once on the report the spies brought back (2:24).

decisions.choice: lodged: stayed overnight
decisions.reason: The verb means to spend the night. Verse 2 says three days passed before the officers gave their orders, so the stay by the river may have lasted more than one night.

decisions.choice: the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable adds "River" at the first mention so that a new reader knows what the Jordan is.

records.heading: Israel comes to the Jordan

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וַיַּעַבְר֥וּ הַשֹּׁטְרִ֖ים בְּקֶ֥רֶב הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was at [the] end of three days, and passed the officers through [the] midst of the camp.
pieces: At the end of three days the officers went throughout the camp.

L.2: And it came about at the end of three days that the officers passed through the midst of the camp.

R.2: After three days, the officers went all through the camp.

decisions.choice: at the end of three days: the time Joshua set in 1:11
decisions.reason: In 1:10-11 Joshua told the officers to tell the people that within three days they would cross the Jordan. This verse takes up that count. The spies also spent three days hiding in the hills (2:22); the chapters do not say exactly how the two sets of days line up.

decisions.choice: officers: officials who passed orders on to the people
decisions.reason: These are the officials Joshua gave orders to in 1:10. The word is used for officials who kept records and saw that orders were carried out among the people (Exodus 5:6; Numbers 11:16; Deuteronomy 20:5).

records.source: וַיְצַוּוּ֮ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹר֒ כִּרְאֽוֹתְכֶ֗ם אֵ֣ת אֲר֤וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם וְהַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם נֹשְׂאִ֖ים אֹת֑וֹ וְאַתֶּ֗ם תִּסְעוּ֙ מִמְּק֣וֹמְכֶ֔ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֖ם אַחֲרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And they commanded the people, saying, when you see [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh your God, and the priests the Levites carrying it, and you, you will set out from your place and go after it.
pieces: They gave the people this order: "As soon as you see the Levitical priests carrying the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, move out from where you are and follow it.

L.3: And they commanded the people, saying, "When you see the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and the priests, the Levites, carrying it, then you shall set out from your place and go after it.

R.3: They told the people, "Watch for the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. It is the sacred box that holds the covenant tablets. When you see the priests from the tribe of Levi carrying it, leave your places and follow it.

decisions.choice: the ark of the covenant: the chest that held the covenant tablets and marked God's presence
decisions.reason: The ark was a wooden chest covered with gold that held the two stone tablets of the covenant (Exodus 25:10-22; Deuteronomy 10:1-5). It went ahead of Israel on the march (Numbers 10:33-36). In this chapter it leads the way into the Jordan, and the people follow it.

decisions.choice: the priests, the Levites: priests who belong to the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: The phrase is common in Deuteronomy (17:9; 18:1). It names the priests by their tribe. Deuteronomy 31:9 speaks of "the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of Yahweh".

decisions.choice: and you, you shall set out: the people move only when the ark moves
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is stressed. The ark goes first, and only then is it the people's turn to move.

decisions.choice: It is the sacred box that holds the covenant tablets.
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word "ark" and explains it once, the first time it appears in this chapter.

decisions.choice: being carried by the Levitical priests
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two things the people will see, the ark and the priests carrying it, into one picture, naming the priests first.

records.source: אַ֣ךְ׀רָח֣וֹק יִהְיֶ֗ה בֵּֽינֵיכֶם֙ וּבֵינָ֔יו כְּאַלְפַּ֥יִם אַמָּ֖ה בַּמִּדָּ֑ה אַֽל־תִּקְרְב֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו לְמַ֤עַן אֲשֶׁר־תֵּֽדְעוּ֙ אֶת־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּֽלְכוּ־בָ֔הּ כִּ֣י לֹ֧א עֲבַרְתֶּ֛ם בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ מִתְּמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃ס
records.gloss: Only a distance there will be between you and between it, about two thousand cubits by measure; do not draw near to it, so that you may know the way which you will go in it, for not you have passed on the way yesterday [and] three days ago.
pieces: But keep a distance of about {{units:3,000 feet|2,000 cubits}} between yourselves and the ark; do not go near it. Then you will know which way to go, since you have never traveled this way before."

L.4: Only there shall be a distance between you and it, about 2,000 cubits by measure; do not come near it, so that you may know the way by which you shall go, for you have not passed on [this] way yesterday [or the day] before."

R.4: But stay about {{units:3,000 feet|2,000 cubits}} behind it. Do not go near it. Then you will be able to see which way to go. You have never been on this road before."

decisions.choice: keep a distance: the ark is holy and not to be approached carelessly
decisions.reason: Only those appointed could come near the ark (Numbers 4:15, 20; 2 Samuel 6:6-7). The distance also let the whole people see the ark ahead of them and follow where it led.

decisions.choice: yesterday and the day before: at any time before now
decisions.reason: The pair of words is a common way of saying "previously" (Genesis 31:2; Exodus 5:7). The people have never traveled this road.

decisions.choice: between it, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the reading the scribes marked (qere) are two spellings of "and between it". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: about 3,000 feet
decisions.reason: A cubit is about 18 inches, so 2,000 cubits is about 3,000 feet, a little over half a mile. The Measures setting shows the original unit; Literal keeps it.

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶל־הָעָ֖ם הִתְקַדָּ֑שׁוּ כִּ֣י מָחָ֗ר יַעֲשֶׂ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֖ם נִפְלָאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And said Joshua to the people, consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow will do Yahweh in your midst wonders.
pieces: Joshua told the people, "Set yourselves apart as holy, because tomorrow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to work wonders among you."

L.5: And Joshua said to the people, "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do wonders in your midst."

R.5: Joshua told the people, "Make yourselves clean and holy. Tomorrow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do amazing things among you."

decisions.choice: consecrate yourselves: get ready for God to act by becoming ritually clean
decisions.reason: Before God appeared at Sinai, the people washed their clothes and kept apart from sexual relations (Exodus 19:10-15). The people here probably prepared in a similar way, because God was about to act among them.

decisions.choice: wonders: deeds beyond human power that only God can do
decisions.reason: The word is used of the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 3:20) and of God's promise when he renewed the covenant (Exodus 34:10). Here it points to the stopping of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: set yourselves apart as holy / make yourselves clean and holy
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself holy. Balanced and Readable spell out that sense; Literal keeps "consecrate".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אֶל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים לֵאמֹ֔ר שְׂאוּ֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הַבְּרִ֔ית וְעִבְר֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וַיִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הַבְּרִ֔ית וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And said Joshua to the priests, saying, lift up [the] ark of the covenant and pass on before the people. And they lifted up [the] ark of the covenant and went before the people.
pieces: Joshua said to the priests, "Take up the ark of the covenant and go across ahead of the people." So they took up the ark of the covenant and went on ahead of the people.

L.6: And Joshua spoke to the priests, saying, "Lift up the ark of the covenant and pass over before the people." And they lifted up the ark of the covenant and went before the people.

R.6: Joshua told the priests, "Pick up the ark of the covenant and go across ahead of the people." So the priests picked up the ark and walked in front of the people.

decisions.choice: pass over: the key verb of the crossing
decisions.reason: The verb "pass over" or "cross" runs through chapters 1-4 (1:2, 11; 3:1, 14, 16, 17; 4:1). Here the priests are to go on ahead and lead the crossing.

decisions.choice: and they lifted up ... and went: the outcome told first
decisions.reason: The verse sums up what the priests did. The full account of their going into the river follows in verses 14-17, after God's words to Joshua. Biblical stories often give the outcome first and then fill in the details.

decisions.choice: the priests
decisions.reason: Readable names the priests as the ones who lifted the ark, and leaves out the repeated "of the covenant".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה אָחֵל֙ גַּדֶּלְךָ֔ בְּעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁר֙ יֵֽדְע֔וּן כִּ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיִ֛יתִי עִם־מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶהְיֶ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Joshua, the day this I will begin to make you great in [the] eyes of all Israel, that they may know that just as I was with Moses, I will be with you.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to raise you up in the sight of all Israel, so that they will know I will be with you as I was with Moses.

L.7: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "This day I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel, that they may know that just as I was with Moses, I will be with you.

R.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to make you a great leader in the eyes of all the people of Israel. Then they will know that I will be with you, just as I was with Moses.

decisions.choice: make you great: give you standing and honor as leader
decisions.reason: The verb means to make great. God will show the people that Joshua is their leader, as he showed it for Moses at the sea (Exodus 14:31). Joshua 4:14 says it came true: the people held Joshua in awe as they had held Moses.

decisions.choice: as I was with Moses, I will be with you: the promise of 1:5
decisions.reason: God made this promise to Joshua in 1:5, and the people repeated it in 1:17. The crossing of the Jordan is the first proof of it, matching the crossing of the sea under Moses.

decisions.choice: a great leader
decisions.reason: Readable says in what way Joshua will be made great: as the leader of the people.

records.heading: I will be with you as I was with Moses

records.source: וְאַתָּ֗ה תְּצַוֶּה֙ אֶת־הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים נֹשְׂאֵ֥י אֲרֽוֹן־הַבְּרִ֖ית לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּבֹאֲכֶ֗ם עַד־קְצֵה֙ מֵ֣י הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן בַּיַּרְדֵּ֖ן תַּעֲמֹֽדוּ׃פ
records.gloss: And you, you will command the priests carrying [the] ark of the covenant, saying, when you come to [the] edge of [the] waters of the Jordan, in the Jordan you will stand.
pieces: Now you are to give an order to the priests who carry the ark of the covenant: 'Once you have reached the edge of the Jordan's waters, stop and stand in the river.'"

L.8: And you, command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant, saying, 'When you come to the edge of the waters of the Jordan, you shall stand still in the Jordan.'"

R.8: Tell the priests who carry the ark of the covenant, 'When you come to the edge of the water of the Jordan, step into the river and stand there.'"

decisions.choice: stand: stop and stay where you are
decisions.reason: The verb means to stand or stand still. The priests are to stop once their feet are in the edge of the water (verse 15) and stay there; in verse 17 they stand firm in the middle of the riverbed.

decisions.choice: and you: God turns from what he will do to what Joshua must do
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed. God has said what he will do for Joshua (verse 7); now he tells Joshua his part.

decisions.choice: step into the river and stand there
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the priests are to go into the water, as verse 15 shows they did, and then stay where they are.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל גֹּ֣שׁוּ הֵ֔נָּה וְשִׁמְע֕וּ אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Joshua to [the] sons of Israel, come near here and hear [the] words of Yahweh your God.
pieces: Joshua said to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "Come over here and listen to the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

L.9: And Joshua said to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, "Come near here and hear the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

R.9: Joshua said to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "Come here and listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God says."

decisions.choice: the words of Yahweh your God: Joshua passes on God's message
decisions.reason: What Joshua says next (verses 10-13) is presented as God's own word, as the words of Moses were. Joshua speaks for God as Moses had done.

records.heading: The waters of the Jordan stop

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ בְּזֹאת֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּן כִּ֛י אֵ֥ל חַ֖י בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וְהוֹרֵ֣שׁ יוֹרִ֣ישׁ מִ֠פְּנֵיכֶם אֶת־הַכְּנַעֲנִ֨י וְאֶת־הַחִתִּ֜י וְאֶת־הַחִוִּ֗י וְאֶת־הַפְּרִזִּי֙ וְאֶת־הַגִּרְגָּשִׁ֔י וְהָאֱמֹרִ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Joshua, by this you will know that [the] living God [is] in your midst, and driving out he will drive out from before you the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Hivite and the Perizzite and the Girgashite and the Amorite and the Jebusite.
pieces: Joshua went on, "Here is the way you will know that the living God is in your midst, and that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will without fail drive out ahead of you the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites.

L.10: And Joshua said, "By this you shall know that the living God [is] in your midst, and that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will surely dispossess from before you the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Hivites and the Perizzites and the Girgashites and the Amorites and the Jebusites.

R.10: Then Joshua said, "This is how you will be sure that the living God is here among you. You will know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will surely drive out the peoples who live in this land: the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites.

decisions.choice: the living God: the God who acts, unlike lifeless idols
decisions.reason: The title sets Israel's God against gods that cannot act (Deuteronomy 5:26; 1 Samuel 17:26; Psalm 115:3-8). The stopping of the Jordan will show that he is present and at work among his people.

decisions.choice: will surely dispossess: a doubled verb that makes the promise certain
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated in two forms, a way of stressing that something will certainly happen. The verb means to dispossess, to drive out those who held the land so that others take it over.

decisions.choice: the seven peoples of Canaan
decisions.reason: The same seven peoples are listed in Deuteronomy 7:1. They lived in the land when Israel arrived; the Canaanites were by the sea and the Amorites in the hill country and beyond (5:1; Numbers 13:29). Each name is singular and stands for the whole people.

decisions.choice: the peoples who live in this land
decisions.reason: Readable says who the seven names are before listing them.

records.source: הִנֵּה֙ אֲר֣וֹן הַבְּרִ֔ית אֲד֖וֹן כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ עֹבֵ֥ר לִפְנֵיכֶ֖ם בַּיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: Look, [the] ark of the covenant of [the] Lord of all the earth [is] passing on before you into the Jordan.
pieces: See, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is going ahead of you into the Jordan.

L.11: Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is passing over before you into the Jordan.

R.11: Look! The ark of the covenant of the Lord of the whole earth is going into the Jordan ahead of you.

decisions.choice: the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth
decisions.reason: The text reads "the ark of the covenant, Lord of all the earth": "covenant" carries the article, and the title follows it. The title is best taken as naming the owner of the ark, as verse 13 says plainly: "the ark of Yahweh, Lord of all the earth".

decisions.choice: the Lord of all the earth: God rules every land, Canaan included
decisions.reason: The title (also verse 13; Micah 4:13; Psalm 97:5) says that Israel's God is master of the whole earth, not the god of one place. He is leading his people into a land he already rules.

decisions.choice: is passing over: about to take place
decisions.reason: The participle describes what is about to happen as if it were already under way.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה קְח֤וּ לָכֶם֙ שְׁנֵ֣י עָשָׂ֣ר אִ֔ישׁ מִשִּׁבְטֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִישׁ־אֶחָ֥ד אִישׁ־אֶחָ֖ד לַשָּֽׁבֶט׃
records.gloss: And now take for yourselves two [and] ten men from [the] tribes of Israel, a man one, a man one for the tribe.
pieces: Now choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man from each tribe.

L.12: And now take for yourselves twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man, one man for each tribe.

R.12: Now choose twelve men, one from each of the twelve tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: take twelve men: their task is told only in chapter 4
decisions.reason: Joshua does not yet say why the men are chosen. In 4:2-7 they carry twelve stones from the riverbed to be a memorial of the crossing.

decisions.choice: one man, one man: one for each
decisions.reason: Repeating the phrase gives the sense "one each": one man from every tribe (Numbers 13:2).

decisions.choice: choose
decisions.reason: The verb is "take"; here it means to select men for a task.

records.source: וְהָיָ֡ה כְּנ֣וֹחַ כַּפּ֣וֹת רַגְלֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֡ים נֹשְׂאֵי֩ אֲר֨וֹן יְהוָ֜ה אֲד֤וֹן כָּל־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ בְּמֵ֣י הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן מֵ֤י הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ יִכָּ֣רֵת֔וּן הַמַּ֥יִם הַיֹּרְדִ֖ים מִלְמָ֑עְלָה וְיַעַמְד֖וּ נֵ֥ד אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when rest [the] soles of [the] feet of the priests carrying [the] ark of Yahweh, Lord of all the earth, in [the] waters of the Jordan, [the] waters of the Jordan will be cut off, the waters coming down from above, and they will stand [as] a heap one.
pieces: The priests carrying the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Lord of all the earth, will set the soles of their feet in the Jordan's waters, and as soon as they do, the waters of the Jordan will be cut off. The water flowing down from upstream will stand up in a single heap."

L.13: And it shall be, when the soles of the feet of the priests who carry the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan will be cut off, the waters coming down from above, and they will stand [in] one heap."

R.13: The priests will carry the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Lord of the whole earth. As soon as their feet touch the water of the Jordan, the river will stop flowing. The water coming down the river will be held back, and it will pile up in one heap."

decisions.choice: stand in one heap: the waters as at the sea
decisions.reason: The word "heap" describes the waters of the sea in Israel's song (Exodus 15:8) and in Psalm 78:13. The crossing of the Jordan repeats the crossing of the sea (4:23).

decisions.choice: be cut off: stop flowing
decisions.reason: The verb means to be cut. The flow from upstream is cut off, so the water below runs away and the riverbed is left dry (verse 16).

decisions.choice: the soles of the feet rest: the moment the priests step into the water
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures the first touch of the priests' feet on the water, as verse 15 tells it.

decisions.choice: the priests' task first, then the promise
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long sentence into short ones, starting with the priests carrying the ark.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בִּנְסֹ֤עַ הָעָם֙ מֵאָ֣הֳלֵיהֶ֔ם לַעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים נֹֽשְׂאֵ֛י הָאָר֥וֹן הַבְּרִ֖ית לִפְנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was, when set out the people from their tents to cross the Jordan, and the priests carrying the ark of the covenant [were] before the people,
pieces: So when the people broke camp to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the ark of the covenant ahead of them,

L.14: And it came about, when the people set out from their tents to cross over the Jordan, with the priests who carried the ark of the covenant before the people,

R.14: The people left their tents to cross the Jordan. The priests carrying the ark of the covenant went ahead of them.

decisions.choice: one sentence running through verses 14-16
decisions.reason: Verses 14 and 15 set the scene with a chain of "when" clauses; the main statement comes in verse 16: the waters stood still.

decisions.choice: set out from their tents: broke camp
decisions.reason: The verb means to pull up the tent pegs and move on. The people left the camp where they had stayed by the river (verses 1-2).

records.source: וּכְב֞וֹא נֹשְׂאֵ֤י הָֽאָרוֹן֙ עַד־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וְרַגְלֵ֤י הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ נֹשְׂאֵ֣י הָֽאָר֔וֹן נִטְבְּל֖וּ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַמָּ֑יִם וְהַיַּרְדֵּ֗ן מָלֵא֙ עַל־כָּל־גְּדוֹתָ֔יו כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י קָצִֽיר׃
records.gloss: and when came those carrying the ark to the Jordan, and [the] feet of the priests carrying the ark were dipped in [the] edge of the waters, and the Jordan is full over all its banks all [the] days of harvest,
pieces: and as soon as the men carrying the ark reached the Jordan and the priests' feet dipped into the edge of the water (the Jordan overflows all its banks throughout the harvest season),

L.15: and when those who carried the ark came to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests who carried the ark were dipped in the edge of the water (now the Jordan overflows all its banks all the days of harvest),

R.15: It was harvest time, when the Jordan floods over all its banks. The priests carrying the ark came to the river, and as soon as their feet touched the edge of the water,

decisions.choice: the days of harvest: spring, when the Jordan is in flood
decisions.reason: The crossing took place in the first month, in spring (4:19), at the time of the barley harvest. Rain and melting snow from the northern mountains then fill the Jordan, and it spreads over its banks (1 Chronicles 12:16). The river was at its hardest to cross.

decisions.choice: the Jordan overflows ...: a note from the narrator
decisions.reason: The clause breaks into the story to tell the reader why the event was so remarkable.

decisions.choice: were dipped: the priests' feet just entered the water
decisions.reason: The verb means to be dipped or plunged. The priests had only stepped into the edge of the water when the river stopped.

decisions.choice: the note about the harvest first
decisions.reason: Readable gives the narrator's note as its own sentence before the moment the priests step in, so the story can run straight on into verse 16.

decisions.choice: the men carrying the ark
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "those carrying the ark"; the same verse names them as the priests.

records.source: וַיַּעַמְד֡וּ הַמַּיִם֩ הַיֹּרְדִ֨ים מִלְמַ֜עְלָה קָ֣מוּ נֵד־אֶחָ֗ד הַרְחֵ֨ק מְאֹ֜ד מֵֽאָדָ֤ם הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מִצַּ֣ד צָֽרְתָ֔ן וְהַיֹּרְדִ֗ים עַ֣ל יָ֧ם הָעֲרָבָ֛ה יָם־הַמֶּ֖לַח תַּ֣מּוּ נִכְרָ֑תוּ וְהָעָ֥ם עָבְר֖וּ נֶ֥גֶד יְרִיחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: and stood the waters coming down from above; they rose up [as] a heap one very far away, at Adam, the city which [is] beside Zarethan; and those going down to [the] sea of the Arabah, [the] sea of the salt, were completely cut off; and the people crossed over opposite Jericho.
pieces: the water flowing down from upstream stopped. It rose up in a single heap a great distance away, at Adam, the town next to Zarethan, while the water running down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Dead Sea, was cut off completely. And the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

L.16: the waters coming down from above stood still; they rose up in one heap very far away, at Adam, the city that [is] beside Zarethan; and those going down toward the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were completely cut off; and the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

R.16: the water coming down the river stopped flowing. It piled up in one heap far up the river, at a town called Adam, near Zarethan. The water flowing down to the Dead Sea was completely cut off. So the people crossed the river near Jericho.

decisions.choice: at Adam
alternatives: the waters rose up in a heap reaching from Adam
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "at Adam"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "from Adam". With "very far away" before it, "from Adam" most likely means the same thing: the heap stood far off, at that town. It could also mean that the piled-up water reached all the way from Adam.

decisions.choice: Adam and Zarethan: towns in the Jordan valley north of the crossing
decisions.reason: Adam is probably the site where the Jabbok River joins the Jordan, some 20 miles upstream from the crossing near Jericho. Zarethan lay near it (1 Kings 7:46). Because the flow was stopped so far upstream, a long stretch of riverbed was left dry.

decisions.choice: the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the deep valley through which the Jordan runs. The sea at its southern end was called the Salt Sea for its very salty water (Genesis 14:3; Deuteronomy 3:17).

decisions.choice: the Dead Sea (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the name by which the sea is known today, as in Numbers 34:3 and Joshua 15:2; Readable leaves out the older name "Sea of the Arabah".

decisions.choice: a town called Adam
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Adam is the name of a town.

records.source: וַיַּעַמְד֣וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֡ים נֹ֠שְׂאֵי הָאָר֨וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֜ה בֶּחָֽרָבָ֛ה בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן הָכֵ֑ן וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עֹֽבְרִים֙ בֶּחָ֣רָבָ֔ה עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר־תַּ֨מּוּ֙ כָּל־הַגּ֔וֹי לַעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And stood the priests carrying the ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh on dry ground in [the] middle of the Jordan firmly, and all Israel [were] crossing on dry ground, until that had finished all the nation crossing the Jordan.
pieces: The priests who bore the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} took a firm stand on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan. Meanwhile all Israel went across on dry ground, until the entire nation had completed the crossing.

L.17: And the priests who carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel was crossing over on dry ground, until the whole nation had finished crossing over the Jordan.

R.17: Holding the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the priests stood still on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan. They stayed there while all the people of Israel walked across on dry ground, until the whole nation had crossed the river.

decisions.choice: dry ground: the word used at the sea
decisions.reason: The same word describes the seabed laid bare at the crossing of the sea (Exodus 14:21). The two crossings mirror each other (4:23).

decisions.choice: firmly: steady, fixed in place
decisions.reason: The word means firmly set. It may describe the priests standing steady, or the firm ground under them; either way the priests held their place in the riverbed until everyone had crossed.

decisions.choice: the whole nation: Israel as one people
decisions.reason: The word often names other nations, but here it names Israel as a people entering its own land, as God promised Abraham (Genesis 12:2).

decisions.choice: They stayed there
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the priests did not move until the crossing was over.
